1. What DataSHIELD and OMOP mean

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-01-mental-model.Rmd
book-01-mental-model.Rmd

What you will learn

Distinguish the database, a private assignment and a released aggregate.

This chapter uses the public synthetic GiBleed practice connection from Getting started. You need: the packages and the matching practice connection described in Before you start. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

Start this chapter

Start a fresh R session in the book-work directory created in Getting started. Run this setup first:

library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
source("tools/book/practice.R")
practice <- if (book_driver == "DSLite") book_practice("gibleed") else book_connect("gibleed")
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

The site connection is ready. The shared connection.R selects DSLite or Opal and resolves the resource names.

A shared table structure

OMOP is a common data model (CDM): a shared set of tables and column meanings. person describes people; visit_occurrence describes visits; observation holds observations and questionnaire answers; death records deaths. A concept is a coded meaning, such as an education answer. A vocabulary supplies its name.

Ask which tables are available:

tables <- ds.omop.tables(conns = conns)
knitr::kable(tables$site)
table_name schema_category has_person_id concept_prefix
person CDM TRUE
observation_period CDM TRUE
visit_occurrence CDM TRUE visit
visit_detail CDM TRUE visit_detail
condition_occurrence CDM TRUE condition
drug_exposure CDM TRUE drug
procedure_occurrence CDM TRUE procedure
device_exposure CDM TRUE device
measurement CDM TRUE measurement
observation CDM TRUE observation
death CDM TRUE
note CDM TRUE
note_nlp CDM FALSE
specimen CDM TRUE specimen
fact_relationship CDM FALSE
location CDM FALSE
care_site CDM FALSE
provider CDM FALSE
payer_plan_period CDM TRUE
cost CDM FALSE
drug_era CDM TRUE
dose_era CDM TRUE
condition_era CDM TRUE
metadata CDM FALSE
cdm_source CDM FALSE
concept Vocabulary FALSE
vocabulary Vocabulary FALSE
domain Vocabulary FALSE
concept_class Vocabulary FALSE
concept_relationship Vocabulary FALSE
relationship Vocabulary FALSE
concept_synonym Vocabulary FALSE
concept_ancestor Vocabulary FALSE
source_to_concept_map Vocabulary FALSE
drug_strength Vocabulary FALSE

These are table names, not records. You can learn the structure without seeing a person’s dates or answers.

Send a question to the data

DataSHIELD sends approved operations to the server. An assignment creates a private object there. An aggregate returns a checked summary. The server can refuse a result that lacks enough supporting people; a refusal is not a zero.

Ask for safe information about the person table:

ds.omop.table.stats("person", conns = conns)$per_site$site
#> $rows
#> [1] 2690
#> 
#> $persons
#> [1] 2690

The displayed 2690 is the lower end of a five-person band: from 2690 through 2694 people. This endpoint rounds down to a multiple of five in the practice configuration; it has not told you the exact count. A later categorical table may release exact supported cells through its own checks. Different endpoints answer different questions and have different disclosure rules.

YouChoose events, variables and outputs.
→
ServerCompute with private records and apply release checks.
→
You seeSymbol names, schemas and checked summaries.

What stays on the server

You never download this book’s assigned person table through DataSHIELD. person_id becomes a pseudonym, but pseudonyms are still private row values. Dates and ages are also private. Coarsening dates helps define a useful analysis; it does not grant permission to fetch rows.

The practical sequence is: choose events, describe variables, assign a table, then request an aggregate. Chapters 5–7 walk through it one small step at a time.

Recap

OMOP makes data structures familiar. DataSHIELD keeps patient rows at the server and checks released summaries.
